findings.title: The duel interior has no fire, oxygen or room-impact signal, so the grade, the hit flash and the vacuum screenshot cannot work there
findings.claim: Sections 5 and 7 assume the duel has the same hull, fire, low-oxygen and room-impact signals as the sector. It does not. d.interior never runs the fire, oxygen or debris systems, and rooms.impactTick is written only by the sector debris code. The duel's hit signal is a ViewEvent with no target room, and its hull lives on the tactical state. So in the duel, alert can only come from hull, vacuum can never happen, 'a white flash on the hit room' has no room to flash, fire lights and embers never appear, and the acceptance screenshot 'duel interior in ... vacuum' cannot be taken without changing sim state.
findings.evidence: spec L49-52, L64, L74; sim/duel/step.ts:L1-2 (the sector step never runs on the interior; only sit, stand, repair and movement), L124; sim/duel/state.ts:L1-2; sim/debris.ts:L117 (the only writer of rooms.impactTick); render/tactical/fxModel.ts:L32-37 (hitsCrew; laser events carry no target), L45; sim/tactical/state.ts:L41, L116 (hull, max from the class)
findings.why: An implementer writing the 'one adapter per mode' has nothing to read for fire, oxygen or the hit room in the duel, so each would invent something different. The stated screenshot gate is impossible.
findings.fix: Name the duel adapter exactly. hull fraction = d.tactical.systems[CREW_SLOT].hull / that class's starting hull. Fire and vacuum are always off in the duel; say so. A hit = hitsCrew(e) over the tick's ViewEvents (the same feed pushEvents gets). The hit room = the repair room (d.points) of the tactical room whose level rose this tick; if no level rose, flash every interior room. Change the screenshot list to duel normal and alert, and sector vacuum.

findings.title: Impact feel does not say whether it replaces or adds to the three existing shake and flash paths
findings.claim: Section 7 specifies a 6 art-pixel shake (0.25 s) and a 2-frame white flash. The code already has a sector shake (3 or 4 internal px over 0.25 s, applied to the world and the projectiles container), a sector red impact flash (18 ticks), and a duel shake (6 px over 0.2 s, applied to the whole duel scene including the readout column and tactical view). The spec does not say whether these are replaced, kept or stacked. It also does not say which container the new shake moves. '2-frame' counts render frames, which depends on the refresh rate (14 ms at 144 Hz), and it is unclear whether those frames count during the 60 ms hitstop.
findings.evidence: spec L64; render/projectileModel.ts:L9; render/projectiles.ts:L96, L122-126; render/renderer.ts:L76; render/effects.ts:L15, L47-54; render/tactical/fxModel.ts:L14, L45, L56-60; app/duel/duelMode.ts:L91-92
findings.why: Two implementers would build different results: double shake, a red-then-white flash, or a shake that also moves the readout panel. 'off removes shake' is undefined if the old shakes survive.
findings.fix: State that the new shake replaces SHAKE_* in projectiles.ts and the duel fxModel shake. Give its target: sector = world plus projectiles container (as today); duel = interior.world only, not the readout. State that the white flash replaces the red impactLayer flash. Define the flash as 2 sim ticks (or 33 ms), not render frames, and say that hitstop does not extend it.

findings.title: The `feel` setting has nowhere to live and no way to change it
findings.claim: The spec adds a `feel` setting (full, reduced, off), but the renderer has no settings store. Menus and the HUD are non-goals, so there is no UI to change it. The spec gives no storage key, default, boot-time read, or test hook.
findings.evidence: spec L13, L64; src/renderer/src/main.ts:L55-58 (the only localStorage uses: crash, telemetry, progress); no settings module under src/renderer/src
findings.why: Implementers would each invent storage and a toggle, or skip it. The 'reduced halves, off removes' rule cannot be checked in the build.
findings.fix: Specify a localStorage key (for example 'ftlite-feel'), default 'full', read once at boot with a try/catch like main.ts L55-58, and a pure feelScale(setting) that unit tests cover. State that there is no menu UI in Art-i (a settings-screen entry is a follow-up), or name the dev key that cycles it.

findings.title: snapWorldScale: the Cutter outcomes are misstated, the ship is not re-centred, and callouts and projectiles still read the unsnapped fit
findings.claim: (a) The Cutter's fit 0.655 snaps to 0.5 at stage 1 (2·0.5·1 = 1, and 0.5 ≥ 0.75·0.655 = 0.491), so it is crisp at stage 1, which the spec does not say, but 24% smaller. At stage 1.5 it keeps fit (not crisp). At 2.5 it is 0.6. The spec says only 'crisp at stage 2 and above'. (b) Below stage 1, which letterbox.ts says is the normal minimum window, 2·fit·stage can be below 1; 'the largest worldScale ≤ fit that makes it whole' is then 0. (c) worldFit centres x,y for fit.scale, so swapping only the scale puts the ship off-centre. (d) callouts, projectile room centres and shot origins take `fit`, and projectile paths are cached at spawn, so a resize that changes the snap leaves shots in flight aimed at stale points. (e) 'World position rounds to whole screen pixels' needs round(x·stage)/stage, because world.position is in internal pixels under a 1.5 stage scale.
findings.evidence: spec L40; render/letterbox.ts:L3-5; render/worldFit.ts:L10-11; render/renderer.ts:L71, L75-76, L84; render/calloutModel.ts:L48; render/projectileModel.ts:L72; render/projectiles.ts:L58, L87; render/duel/interiorView.ts:L49-50
findings.why: The unit test the spec asks for ('each stage scale, each ship') has no agreed expected values. A literal build shifts the ship and misplaces callouts and enemy-shot targets in ordinary sector play.
findings.fix: Define snapWorldScale(fit, stage) → n = floor(2·fit·stage); if n ≥ 1 and n/(2·stage) ≥ 0.75·fit, scale = n/(2·stage), else scale = fit. Have worldFit and duelFit take the stage scale and return the snapped {scale, x, y}, re-centred in the band, with x,y rounded so x·stage is whole. Pass that same object to callouts.draw and projectiles.draw. Put the expected table in the spec: Skiff and duel 1 at stages 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3; Cutter 0.5, 0.655 (kept), 0.5, 0.6, 0.5. Note the 24% Cutter shrink at stage 1 as accepted, or change the 0.75 rule.

findings.title: The procedural walls and doors are off the art-pixel grid, so 'one pixel size' and 'crisp' are false for them
findings.claim: Walls and door panels are 11 world units thick at offset 10, which is 5.5 art pixels. Jambs start at BAND-3, the seal bar is 3 units high, held ticks are 3 wide, the door outline stroke is 1 world unit (half an art pixel), and vent specks are 4x4 at fractional centres. When the Cutter snaps to 1 screen px per art pixel, the 11-unit band renders 5.5 px and rounds unevenly. Section 4 also writes '1 px' light and shadow edges without saying whether that is a world pixel or an art pixel.
findings.evidence: spec L9, L18, L41; render/doorModel.ts:L8, L29-33; render/wallModel.ts:L26; render/tiles.ts:L43; render/effects.ts:L102-103
findings.why: The headline goal (one pixel size) is not met by the layers this spec recolours, and implementers would pick different units for the new edges.
findings.fix: State that procedural geometry uses whole art pixels (2 world units): PANEL_THICK 10 or 12 with BAND to match, jamb, tick, bar and stroke sizes even, and the '1 px' edges = 1 art pixel = 2 world units. Add a unit test that every wallPicture and doorPicture rect has even x, y, w and h.

findings.title: No signal exists for 'a crew member repairing or fighting fire', or for 'sector systems below full'
findings.claim: SimState has no per-crew working flag. The sector's repair progress is stored per target (fire, breach, station), and whether a player is holding Interact is not in state; interactTarget only says what a crew member would act on. 'Fighting fire' in the sector is the same Repair-fire interaction. The sector has no system health: stations.level is the power allocation, and failed is a binary flag that the fx.arc already shows. The duel has per-player repairWork events, but they are cleared every tick, and the duel has no fire.
findings.evidence: spec L59-60; src/renderer/src/sim/components.ts (Position, Health, Life, Stable, Owner, Seated only); render/hudModel.ts:L226-231; sim/interact.ts:L149-161; sim/state.ts:L43; sim/duel/state.ts:L15-20; render/effects.ts:L106-117
findings.why: Implementers would each invent a heuristic, or reach for input state the renderer does not have in the sector.
findings.fix: Define the derivations. Sector working = conscious, unseated, interactTarget(state,pid).kind in {Fire, Breach, Power}, and that target's progress rose since the last tick (kept in RenderMemory); foam when the kind is Fire, sparks otherwise. Duel working = a repairWork event for that player in d.events of the latest tick. Sector damaged system = stations.failed[i] === 1, and say whether sparks add to or replace the fx.arc.

findings.title: The paid licence class does not fit the manifest schema, the notices or the fallback as described
findings.claim: (a) The file regex accepts only raw/ or art/, so paid/ files fail to parse. (b) LICENSE_URLS is a Record over every licence except 'original', so adding 'paid' forces a URL entry. buildNotices prints LICENSE_URLS[lic] in the heading and the Licence line, which would read 'paid (undefined)'. (c) The spec does not say whether 'required: false' and 'source is the store URL' are enforced in superRefine. (d) 'Falls back exactly as optional art does today (featureReady)' only works for names registered as optional in ASSET_NAMES and grouped in FEATURE_NAMES; house.floor.0..3 is in neither. (e) A paid entry that rebinds an existing free name silently overrides it by manifest order, with no rule. So the goal 'paid art drops in without code changes' is false for any name not already registered.
findings.evidence: spec L9, L26-28, L42; render/manifest.ts:L13, L28-44; render/licenses.ts:L2, L8-15; render/creditsText.ts:L16, L19-24; render/fallback.ts:L4-19; render/assets.ts:L61-71, L76, L86-87; render/assetNames.ts:L9-25; .gitignore:L1-14 (no paid/ yet)
findings.why: Implementers would differ on the notices text, the validation rules and whether paid art may override free names. The 'without code changes' outcome cannot be tested.
findings.fix: Spell out the changes: regex ^(raw|art|paid)/; 'paid' is excluded from LICENSE_URLS like 'original', and notices print 'Licence: paid (commercial licence, <licenseUrl ?? source>)'. superRefine: paid ⇒ file starts with paid/, required false, credit, retrieved, and source a URL; paid/ ⇒ licence paid. Register house.floor.0..3 as optional plus a 'houseFloor' feature. Choose a rule for overrides (forbid two entries binding one name, or 'paid entries listed after free ones win'). Narrow the goal to 'drops in for names Art-i registers'. Add public/assets/paid/ to .gitignore.

findings.title: gradeModel's three states overlap and its thresholds are undefined
findings.claim: The spec lists normal, alert and vacuum as if they were one state. Vacuum is per room and alert is ship-wide, and a single hit often causes both a fire and a breach. The spec does not say whether gradeModel returns an enum or flags. 'The low-oxygen threshold' is ambiguous because two exist (render 0.98, HUD_LOW_O2_FRAC). The blue tint's alpha curve and blend (normal, like today's o2Layer, or multiply in the grade) are not given.
findings.evidence: spec L49-52; render/effects.ts:L12-14, L41-46; render/hudModel.ts:L216; sim/debris.ts:L103-109
findings.why: Two implementers would produce different gradeModel signatures and different 'gradeModel per state' tests (L72).
findings.fix: Specify gradeModel(input) → { alert: boolean; pulse: 0..1; vacuum: { room: number; strength: number }[] }, with alert and vacuum independent. Threshold = LOW_O2_THRESHOLD (0.98). Strength = LOW_O2_MAX_ALPHA·(1−frac), as today. The blue tint replaces LOW_O2_COLOR in o2Layer with normal blend.

findings.title: The layer order omits real containers and contradicts the section's opening line
findings.claim: L46 describes one new layer 'over the ship and under the callouts', but L53 splits it into a multiply grade above the tiles and additive lights at the top of the world. The stated order leaves out the sector magazine layer and the duel's damage tint, markers and labels. Additive lights placed after the duel's labels would wash out the repair labels. The amber and red damage tint (alpha 0.28) also stacks with the red alert pulse.
findings.evidence: spec L46, L53; render/renderer.ts:L53; render/duel/interiorView.ts:L43-45, L55-65
findings.why: Implementers would place lights differently in the duel, and the repair labels and markers may become unreadable.
findings.fix: Give both exact addChild orders. Sector: tiles, grade, effects.below, icons, consoleDesks, magazine, crew, boarders, effects.above, lights. Duel: tiles, grade, effects.below, icons, desks, damage, crew, boarders, effects.above, lights, marks, labels. Reword L46 to match.

findings.title: How the palette loads, how roles map to it, and how the import script fails are unspecified
findings.claim: palette.json lives in public/ and is 'read by the renderer', but the spec does not say whether that is a runtime fetch (async, with a failure mode, while FLOOR, WALL and DOOR_FILL are module constants) or a build-time import. Roles map to palette indices, so swapping in a palette of different size or order (32-48 colours) does not 'recolour everything' sensibly. The import script has no stated behaviour when FTLITE_ASSETS is missing, a pack file is missing, or a frame rectangle is out of bounds. The contact sheet goes to out/, which electron-builder packages whole.
findings.evidence: spec L19, L32-34, L41; render/tiles.ts:L13; render/doorModel.ts:L5; electron-builder.yml:L6 (out/**/*); electron.vite.config.ts:L16, L22
findings.why: Implementers would choose differently between async and static loading. A palette swap could silently map roles to the wrong colours. A half-failed import could leave partial PNGs in paid/.
findings.fix: Make palette.json hold { colours: hex[], roles: { floor: hex, ... } }, imported statically (a swap means a rebuild), with a test that every role colour is in colours. The import validates everything first, then writes, and exits non-zero listing every problem. Put the contact sheet in a gitignored directory outside out/ (for example .art/contact.png).

findings.title: The ambient-life requirements name things the layout does not have
findings.claim: The ship layout has no 'wall vents' (cells are only wall, door, floor or space, and walls are procedural bands), so the steam-puff sources are undefined. Alarm and flicker lamps are 'one per room' with no position rule. The starfield goes 'behind the hull in space tiles', but space cells are not drawn and the world band is not a tile grid, and 'two speeds' has nothing to move relative to, since the interior is stationary. 'Seeded schedule' does not name the seed source.
findings.why: Each implementer would invent placement and the parallax rule. The owner gate would judge arbitrary choices.
findings.fix: Define the placement. Lamp = the room's top-left interior tile, at a fixed art-pixel offset. Vents = wall tiles adjacent to floor, picked by hash(tile) < k. Starfield = a container under the world that fills WORLD_BAND (or INTERIOR_BAND), with the layers drifting at fixed px/s. Seed = hash(layoutHash, run seed), read-only.

findings.title: Too much for one plan; split into pipeline and pixel-perfect, then light and feel
findings.claim: Eight sections cover a script toolchain (pngjs, a perceptual remap), schema and licence changes, a world-fit change across two views, recolouring three layers, a blend-mode grade, a pooled particle system with six emitters, impact feel with a new setting, and ambient life. Several depend on decisions not yet made (the palette, adapter signals). The process tier allows one impl review.
findings.why: A single plan executed by fresh subagents with one impl review risks a large, hard-to-review diff, and the owner's look gate mixes the foundations with the feel.
findings.fix: Split it. Art-i-a: bible, palette and roles, paid manifest, import script, snapped fit with the even-grid procedural art. Art-i-b: grade and lights, particles, impact feel, feel setting, ambient life. Each gets its own owner look.

verified: Skiff 18x9 = 576x288 world px in WORLD_BAND 608x296 gives fit min(1, 1.056, 1.028) = 1, so 2·1·stage is whole at stages 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 (worldFit.ts:L4, L10).
Duel band = 1280−220 = 1060 x 720 (interiorModel.ts:L8-10; resolution.ts:L4-6); a 29x13 Cutter (928x416) fits at scale 1, so the duel interior is crisp at stages 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 as the spec says.
Cutter fit = 608/928 = 0.655 (the height ratio 296/416 = 0.712 is larger); the snapped values at stages 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 and 3 are 0.5, kept fit, 0.5, 0.6 and 0.5 under spec L40's rule.
The starter ship (25x12, fit 0.76) is not crisp at stage 1 (0.5 < 0.57) but stays out of app play: fleet.ts:L1-3 flies only the Skiff and the Cutter.

Sector signals exist: state.hull (state.ts:L28) against HULL_MAX, rooms.fire, rooms.o2 / derived.volume (effects.ts:L43), and rooms.impactTick written on each debris or shot impact (debris.ts:L117), read by effects.ts:L47-54.

Determinism boundary: no module under sim, authority, net, clientControl, headless or events imports from render/ (grep), and the boundary test roots do not include render/ (tests/boundary.test.ts:L12), so a render-owned seeded particle RNG and performance.now timing stay outside the deterministic graph. Nothing in sections 5-8 as written needs a sim write.

The renderer's world container order is tiles, effects.below, icons, consoleDesks, magazine, crew, boarders, effects.above (renderer.ts:L53); the duel's is tiles, effects.below, icons, desks, damage, crew, boarders, effects.above, marks, labels (interiorView.ts:L45). Fire and the low-O2 tint sit in effects.below, so a grade placed under effects.below leaves crew, consoles and hazards untinted as the spec claims.
Textures load with nearest scaling (assets.ts:L27-28) and the app inits with antialias false and roundPixels true (renderer.ts:L36).
Optional assets that fail to load only warn (assets.ts:L67-69), so absent paid files with required false do not stop startup, in dev or packaged builds.
not_verified: Pixi 8.19 blend modes: I believe 'multiply' and 'add' are built-in WebGL blend modes and only the advanced modes need 'pixi.js/advanced-blend-modes', but I did not read node_modules (out of bounds), so the plan should confirm this.
Whether Pixi 8 roundPixels also snaps Graphics vertices, as well as sprites, in this version; not checked in the library source.
The Cutter's 29x13 size: taken from the brief, not counted from cutter.json rows.

Read outside the manifest: sim/duel/step.ts, sim/duel/state.ts, sim/tactical/state.ts, render/tactical/fxModel.ts, app/duel/duelMode.ts, sim/debris.ts, hudModel.ts, sim/interact.ts, wallModel.ts, projectileModel.ts, calloutModel.ts, fleet.ts, electron-builder.yml and electron.vite.config.ts. Findings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 10 needed them.
The research report (reports/Premium pixel art and VFX.md) was not read; no finding depends on it.
Whether a test asserts that every manifest-bound name isKnownName; not looked for. It would make the house.floor registration in finding 7 mandatory rather than advisable.
Whether electron-vite empties out/ on each build, which would delete the contact sheet; not checked.
